rationale:
Split along the structure of Simon's printed proof of Lemma 8.1.3, which the supplied proof elaborates. The selected statement combines four separate obligations.
(A) Printed (1)–(2): differentiate the β-weighted slice measure γ_β(B) = ∫_{Gₙ(B)} β dV with respect to μ_V, and identify it through Radon–Nikodym. This is child slice_density; both (C) and (D) use it.
(B) Printed (3)–(4) plus the Riesz step. This part involves no varifold: if probability measures on the compact space G(N,n) have convergent integrals on a dense subset of C(G), they converge weakly to a probability measure. This is child riesz_limit.
(C) The first part of the lemma, pointwise a.e. This is child pointwise_measure (supplied steps 1–4): a dense sequence, the common null set, and slice measures, then (A) and (B).
(D) The second part, for any η that satisfies the first part. This is child identity_of_limits (supplied step 5): (A) together with uniqueness of limits, which is the printed "e(x,j) is exactly η̃^(x)(β_j)".

- (ii) is identity_of_limits applied to this η and (i).
- Step 0 needs no separate case: if n > N then G = ∅, V = 0 and μ_V = 0.

subproblems.title: Lemma 8.1.3, printed (1)–(2): differentiation of the β-weighted slices of V
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (β : C(Grassmannian N n, ℝ)), (∀ S, 0 ≤ β S) → ∃ e : Euclidean N → ℝ, Measurable e ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ ↦ (∫ z in closedBall x ρ ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)), β z.2 ∂V.measure) / (V.weight (closedBall x ρ)).toReal) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (e x))) ∧ ∀ A : Set (Euclidean N), MeasurableSet A → ∫⁻ z in A ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)), ENNReal.ofReal (β z.2) ∂V.measure = ∫⁻ x in A, ENNReal.ofReal (e x) ∂V.weight
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 8, proof of Lemma 1.3 (p. 207), for a single β = β_j ∈ 𝒦⁺. The printed text reads: "By the XXX Theorem 3.23 of Ch. 1 we know that (since there is a Radon measure γ_j on ℝ^{n+ℓ} characterized by γ_j(B) = ∫_{Gₙ(B)} β_j(S) dV(y,S) for Borel sets B ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ}) (1) e(x,j) = lim_{ρ↓0} ∫_{Gₙ(B_ρ(x))} β_j(S) dV(y,S) / μ_V(B_ρ(x)) exists for each x ∈ ℝ^{n+ℓ} ∖ Z_j, where Z_j is a Borel set with μ_V(Z_j) = 0 and e(x,j) is a μ_V-measurable function of x, with (2) ∫_A e(x,j) dμ_V(x) = ∫_{Gₙ(A)} β_j(S) dV(y,S) for any Borel set A." Correction (a) of the parent proof is applied: μ_V is only Radon on the open set U, not necessarily locally finite at ∂U, so the differentiation theorem is applied on U, where both measures are Radon.

Notation. G := G(N,n), a compact space. μ := μ_V = V.weight, so μ(A) = V(A × G) for Borel A (Varifold.weight_apply). c := sup_G |β| = ‖β‖ < ∞, so 0 ≤ β(S) ≤ c for all S. We use three facts:
(F1) μ(ℝ^N ∖ U) = V((ℝ^N∖U) × G) = 0 (field V.supported);
(F2) μ(K) = V(K × G) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Varifold.weight_finite_on_compact);
(F3) μ is σ-finite (instance Varifold.weight.instSigmaFinite).

1. The measure γ (the printed γ_j). Let F(y,S) := ofReal(β(S)) ∈ [0,∞), a Borel function on ℝ^N × G. Put γ := π_#(V⌞F) with π(y,S) = y, i.e. γ := (V.measure.withDensity F).map Prod.fst. For Borel B ⊆ ℝ^N we have π⁻¹(B) = B × G, so γ(B) = ∫⁻_{B×G} ofReal(β(S)) dV(y,S) (Measure.map_apply, withDensity_apply, Set.prod_univ).

2. Comparison with μ. For Borel B, ofReal(β(S)) ≤ ofReal(c) gives γ(B) ≤ ofReal(c)·V(B × G) = ofReal(c)·μ(B) (lintegral_mono, setLIntegral_const). Hence γ(ℝ^N ∖ U) = 0 by (F1), and γ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U by (F2). Also γ ≪ μ, since μ(B) = 0 forces γ(B) = 0 for Borel B (Measure.AbsolutelyContinuous.mk).

3. γ is the zero extension of a Radon measure on U. Let γ_U := γ.comap Subtype.val be the restriction of γ to the open subspace U, so γ_U(C) = γ(C) for Borel C ⊆ U.
(a) γ_U.map Subtype.val = γ⌞U = γ, because γ(ℝ^N∖U) = 0 (map_comap_subtype_coe, Measure.restrict_eq_self_of_ae_mem).
(b) γ_U is locally finite. U is an open subset of ℝ^N, hence locally compact (IsOpen.locallyCompactSpace), so each y ∈ U has a compact neighbourhood C in U (exists_compact_mem_nhds). Its image in ℝ^N is a compact subset of U, so γ_U(C) = γ(C) < ∞ by step 2.
(c) γ is σ-finite: it is the push-forward of the locally finite, hence σ-finite, measure γ_U on the second-countable space U under the measurable embedding Subtype.val (MeasurableEmbedding.sigmaFinite_map).

4. Differentiation (printed (1); Ch. 1, 3.23(i)). Apply the Besicovitch differentiation theorem on the open set U to the Radon measures γ_U and μ_U := V.domainWeight. Every satellite configuration in the metric subspace U is also one in ℝ^N, so U has the Besicovitch covering property, and closed balls of U are traces of closed balls of ℝ^N. Transporting back along the inclusion, using γ_U.map val = γ and μ_U.map val = μ, gives: for μ-a.e. x,
 γ(B_ρ(x)) / μ(B_ρ(x)) → g(x) := (dγ/dμ)(x) in [0,∞] as ρ ↓ 0,
 where dγ/dμ = γ.rnDeriv μ and the quotients are in [0,∞] with a/b = a·b⁻¹.
 This is exactly the kernel-checked SimonGMT lemma Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter08.Varifold.ae_tendsto_firstVariationDensity_of_domainMeasure V γ_U (FirstVariationDensity.lean:60; it uses hasBesicovitchCovering_subtype, :30). It is in the import closure of GMT.Ch08.Submission and uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. After rewriting γ_U.map Subtype.val = γ by 3(a), its conclusion reads: ∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, Tendsto (fun r ↦ γ (closedBall x r) / V.weight (closedBall x r)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (γ.rnDeriv V.weight x)).
 Mathematically equivalent route (supplied detail (a)): apply Besicovitch's theorem (Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_rnDeriv) to the finite measures γ⌞K and μ⌞K for compact K ⊆ U, at points of interior K, where small closed balls lie in K. Identify d(γ⌞K)/d(μ⌞K) = dγ/dμ μ⌞K-a.e. by uniqueness of the Lebesgue decomposition (Measure.eq_rnDeriv), and use countably many such K whose interiors cover U.
 Moreover g(x) < ∞ for μ-a.e. x, since γ is σ-finite (Measure.rnDeriv_lt_top). Define e(x) := g(x).toReal ∈ [0,∞). Then e is Borel measurable (Measure.measurable_rnDeriv, Measurable.ennreal_toReal).

5. The real quotient: proof of (1). By step 4 and (F1), μ-a.e. x satisfies three conditions at once: x ∈ U, γ(B_ρ(x))/μ(B_ρ(x)) → g(x), and g(x) < ∞. Fix such an x and choose r > 0 with ball(x,r) ⊆ U.
 Let 0 < ρ < r and B := B_ρ(x). Then B ⊆ ball(x,r) ⊆ U is compact, so μ(B) = V(B × G) < ∞ by (F2). The function z ↦ β(z.2) is continuous, ≥ 0 and bounded by c, hence integrable on B × G for V (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded). Therefore
 γ(B) = ∫⁻_{B×G} ofReal(β(z.2)) dV = ofReal(∫_{B×G} β(z.2) dV) (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal),
 and since the integral is ≥ 0, γ(B).toReal = ∫_{B×G} β(z.2) dV (ENNReal.toReal_ofReal). Because (a/b).toReal = a.toReal / b.toReal for all a, b ∈ [0,∞] (ENNReal.toReal_div), for every ρ ∈ (0, r):
 (∫_{B_ρ(x)×G} β(z.2) dV) / μ(B_ρ(x)).toReal = (γ(B_ρ(x)) / μ(B_ρ(x))).toReal.
 Since g(x) ≠ ∞ and toReal is continuous at finite points (ENNReal.tendsto_toReal), (γ(B_ρ(x))/μ(B_ρ(x))).toReal → g(x).toReal = e(x) as ρ ↓ 0. Since (0, r) ∈ 𝓝[>]0, the real quotient has the same limit (Tendsto.congr'). This proves (1).

6. The integral identity: proof of (2). γ ≪ μ by step 2, and γ, μ are σ-finite by 3(c) and (F3). The Radon–Nikodym theorem gives μ⌞g = γ (Measure.withDensity_rnDeriv_eq), i.e. γ(A) = ∫⁻_A g dμ for every Borel A (withDensity_apply). Since g < ∞ μ-a.e., g(x) = ofReal(g(x).toReal) = ofReal(e(x)) for μ-a.e. x (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal). Hence ∫⁻_A g dμ = ∫⁻_A ofReal(e) dμ (setLIntegral_congr_fun_ae). With step 1, ∫⁻_{A×G} ofReal(β(S)) dV = γ(A) = ∫⁻_A ofReal(e(x)) dμ(x). This is (2), the printed (2) written as an identity of lintegrals. ∎
proof_key_steps: γ(B) := ∫⁻_{B×G} ofReal β dV is the Borel measure π_#(V⌞ofReal∘β∘snd) on ℝ^N with γ ≤ ‖β‖·μ_V; hence γ vanishes off U, is finite on compact subsets of U, and γ ≪ μ_V.
γ is the zero extension of the locally finite measure γ.comap Subtype.val on U, hence σ-finite.
Besicovitch differentiation on U (SimonGMT Varifold.ae_tendsto_firstVariationDensity_of_domainMeasure): γ(B_ρ(x))/μ_V(B_ρ(x)) → dγ/dμ_V(x) < ∞ for μ_V-a.e. x; set e := toReal(dγ/dμ_V).
For x ∈ U and small ρ, the real Bochner quotient equals toReal of the [0,∞] ratio (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal, ENNReal.toReal_div); this gives (1).
Radon–Nikodym gives μ_V⌞(dγ/dμ_V) = γ, and dγ/dμ_V = ofReal∘e μ_V-a.e.; this gives (2).

subproblems.title: Weak limit on G(N,n) from convergence on a dense set (printed (3)–(4) and the Riesz step of Lemma 8.1.3)
subproblems.statement: Let G = G(N,n), a compact Hausdorff second-countable space with its Borel σ-algebra. Let l be a nontrivial filter on ℝ, and (m_ρ)_{ρ∈ℝ} Borel measures on G such that m_ρ is a probability measure for l-eventually all ρ. Let D ⊆ C(G,ℝ) be dense for the sup-norm topology (the topology of C(G,ℝ), as G is compact), and suppose lim_l ∫ f dm_ρ exists in ℝ for every f ∈ D. Then there is a Borel probability measure η on G with ∫ f dm_ρ → ∫ f dη along l for every f ∈ C(G,ℝ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (l : Filter ℝ) (m : ℝ → Measure (Grassmannian N n)) (D : Set C(Grassmannian N n, ℝ)), l.NeBot → (∀ᶠ ρ in l, IsProbabilityMeasure (m ρ)) → Dense D → (∀ f ∈ D, ∃ c : ℝ, Tendsto (fun ρ ↦ ∫ S, f S ∂(m ρ)) l (𝓝 c)) → ∃ η : Measure (Grassmannian N n), IsProbabilityMeasure η ∧ ∀ f : C(Grassmannian N n, ℝ), Tendsto (fun ρ ↦ ∫ S, f S ∂(m ρ)) l (𝓝 (∫ S, f S ∂η))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 8, proof of Lemma 1.3: printed (3), (4) and the final appeal to the Riesz representation theorem, isolated from the varifold. In the book, m_ρ is the normalized slice measure of V over B_ρ(x) and D is the countable dense family. Correction (b) of the parent proof is applied: the limit functional is positive and takes the value 1 at the constant 1, so the Riesz theorem for positive functionals on the compact space G (Ch. 1, 4.12) represents it by a probability measure.

Notation: ‖f‖ = sup_G |f| for f ∈ C(G,ℝ); the metric of C(G,ℝ) is dist(f,g) = ‖f − g‖.

1. Integrability and the estimate (printed (3)). Each f ∈ C(G,ℝ) is continuous on the compact space G, hence bounded (|f(S)| ≤ ‖f‖) and Borel. So it is integrable for every finite Borel measure on G (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport with HasCompactSupport.of_compactSpace). If m is a probability measure and f, g ∈ C(G,ℝ), then
 |∫ f dm − ∫ g dm| = |∫ (f − g) dm| ≤ ‖f − g‖ · m(G) = ‖f − g‖
 (integral_sub; norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const with |(f − g)(S)| ≤ ‖f − g‖, ContinuousMap.norm_coe_le_norm).

2. The limit exists for every f (printed (4)). Fix f ∈ C(G,ℝ), put F(ρ) := ∫ f dm_ρ, and let ε > 0. By density choose g ∈ D with ‖f − g‖ < ε/4 (Dense.exists_dist_lt), and let c_g := lim_l ∫ g dm_ρ.
 For l-eventually all ρ, m_ρ is a probability measure and |∫ g dm_ρ − c_g| < ε/4. For such ρ, step 1 gives |F(ρ) − c_g| ≤ |F(ρ) − ∫ g dm_ρ| + |∫ g dm_ρ − c_g| < ε/4 + ε/4 = ε/2.
 Thus F⁻¹(ball(c_g, ε/2)) ∈ l, i.e. ball(c_g, ε/2) belongs to the image filter F_*(l), and any two points of this ball are at distance < ε. Since l ≠ ⊥, also F_*(l) ≠ ⊥, so F_*(l) is a Cauchy filter on ℝ (Metric.cauchy_iff). As ℝ is complete, F converges along l to a real number L(f) (cauchy_map_iff_exists_tendsto). The printed argument phrases this as limsup − liminf ≤ 2ε for every ε.

3. Properties of L. Limits along the nontrivial filter l in the Hausdorff space ℝ are unique (tendsto_nhds_unique).
(i) Additivity: for l-eventually all ρ, m_ρ is a probability measure, so f and g are integrable and ∫ (f + g) dm_ρ = ∫ f dm_ρ + ∫ g dm_ρ (integral_add). The right side tends to L(f) + L(g), so L(f + g) = L(f) + L(g).
(ii) Homogeneity: ∫ (a f) dm_ρ = a ∫ f dm_ρ for all ρ (integral_smul), so L(a f) = a L(f).
(iii) Monotonicity (positivity): if f ≤ g pointwise, then ∫ f dm_ρ ≤ ∫ g dm_ρ for l-eventually all ρ (integral_mono), so L(f) ≤ L(g) (le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto).
(iv) Normalization: ∫ 1 dm_ρ = m_ρ(G) = 1 for l-eventually all ρ, so L(1) = 1.

4. Riesz representation (Ch. 1, 4.12). G is compact, so every f ∈ C(G,ℝ) has compact support and C(G,ℝ) = C_c(G,ℝ) (HasCompactSupport.of_compactSpace). By step 3, Λ(f) := L(f) is a positive (monotone) linear functional Λ : C_c(G,ℝ) → ℝ. G is a compact Hausdorff (so locally compact T2) space and its σ-algebra is Borel (Subtype.borelSpace). The Riesz–Markov–Kakutani theorem therefore gives a Borel measure η on G with ∫ f dη = Λ(f) = L(f) for all f ∈ C(G,ℝ) (Mathlib RealRMK.rieszMeasure Λ and RealRMK.integral_rieszMeasure, RieszMarkovKakutani/Real.lean:345).
 η is finite because G is compact (instance at Real.lean:445). Also η(G).toReal = ∫ 1 dη = L(1) = 1 (integral_const), so η(G) = 1 and η is a probability measure.

5. Conclusion. For every f ∈ C(G,ℝ), ∫ f dm_ρ → L(f) = ∫ f dη along l, by steps 2 and 4. ∎
proof_key_steps: For a probability measure m: |∫ f dm − ∫ g dm| ≤ ‖f − g‖ (printed (3)).
Approximating f by some g ∈ D whose limit exists shows that ρ ↦ ∫ f dm_ρ is Cauchy along l, so it converges to some L(f) (printed (4)).
L is linear and monotone with L(1) = 1 (limits of eventual identities, uniqueness of limits).
Riesz–Markov–Kakutani on the compact space G (C(G,ℝ) = C_c(G,ℝ)) gives η with ∫ f dη = L(f), and η(G) = L(1) = 1.

subproblems.title: Lemma 8.1.3, first part: the plane-distribution measures η_V^(x) exist μ_V-a.e.
subproblems.statement: Let V be an n-varifold on an open set U ⊆ ℝ^N with weight μ_V. Then for μ_V-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^N there is a Borel probability measure η on G = G(N,n) such that, for every continuous β : G → ℝ, (∫_{B_ρ(x)×G} β(S) dV(y,S)) / μ_V(B_ρ(x)) → ∫ β dη as ρ ↓ 0. Here B_ρ(x) is the closed ball, and the quotient is the Bochner integral divided by the real number μ_V(B_ρ(x)).toReal, with t/0 = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U), ∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, ∃ η : Measure (Grassmannian N n), IsProbabilityMeasure η ∧ ∀ β : C(Grassmannian N n, ℝ), Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ ↦ (∫ z in closedBall x ρ ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)), β z.2 ∂V.measure) / (V.weight (closedBall x ρ)).toReal) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (∫ S, β S ∂η))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 8, proof of Lemma 1.3 (pp. 207–208), first part: the countable dense family, printed (1), (3), (4) and the Riesz step. It follows steps 1–4 of the parent proof. The differentiation (1) is the sibling slice_density; the passage through (3), (4) and Riesz is the sibling riesz_limit.

Notation. G := G(N,n), μ := μ_V = V.weight, and ‖f‖ := sup_G |f| for f ∈ C(G,ℝ). For x ∈ ℝ^N, ρ ∈ ℝ and β ∈ C(G,ℝ) let
 avg_ρ^x(β) := (∫_{B_ρ(x)×G} β(z.2) dV(z)) / μ(B_ρ(x)).toReal,
 which is exactly the quotient in the statement.

1. Countable dense family (printed "β_1, β_2, … ∈ 𝒦⁺ dense in 𝒦⁺"). G is compact and second countable, so C(G,ℝ) (compact-open = sup-norm topology) is second countable, hence separable (Mathlib ContinuousMap.instSeparableSpace, Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/SecondCountableSpace.lean:108). That pure-Mathlib module is not in the contract's import closure and must be imported. Choose f_1, f_2, … with dense range in C(G,ℝ) (TopologicalSpace.exists_dense_seq).
 Put c_j := ‖f_j‖ and β_j := f_j + c_j, adding the constant function c_j. Then β_j ∈ C(G,ℝ) and β_j ≥ 0, since f_j(S) ≥ −|f_j(S)| ≥ −‖f_j‖. This is the printed passage between 𝒦⁺ and 𝒦 via β = (β + c) − c, applied to a dense sequence of 𝒦.

2. Differentiation (printed (1)). For each j, the sibling lemma slice_density applied to V and β_j ≥ 0 gives e_j : ℝ^N → ℝ such that avg_ρ^x(β_j) → e_j(x) as ρ ↓ 0 for μ-a.e. x.

3. A common conull set (the printed x ∈ ℝ^{n+ℓ} ∖ ⋃_j Z_j). Each condition below holds for μ-a.e. x. There are countably many of them, so they hold simultaneously for μ-a.e. x (ae_all_iff, filter_upwards).
(a) x ∈ U, because μ(ℝ^N∖U) = V((ℝ^N∖U) × G) = 0 (Varifold.weight_apply, V.supported).
(b) x ∈ spt μ, i.e. μ(W) > 0 for every neighbourhood W of x. ℝ^N is second countable, hence hereditarily Lindelöf, so μ(ℝ^N ∖ spt μ) = 0 (Measure.support_mem_ae, Support.lean:198; Measure.mem_support_iff_forall, :75).
(c) For every j, avg_ρ^x(β_j) → e_j(x) as ρ ↓ 0 (step 2).
 Fix such an x; it remains to produce η for it.

4. Small balls. U is open and x ∈ U, so choose r > 0 with ball(x,r) ⊆ U. For 0 < ρ < r, B_ρ(x) ⊆ ball(x,r) ⊆ U is compact, so μ(B_ρ(x)) < ∞ (Varifold.weight_finite_on_compact). Also μ(B_ρ(x)) ≥ μ(ball(x,ρ)) > 0 by (b), because the open ball ball(x,ρ) is a neighbourhood of x.

5. Slice measures. For ρ ∈ ℝ define the Borel measure on G
 m_ρ := μ(B_ρ(x))⁻¹ · σ_#(V⌞(B_ρ(x) × G)), with σ(y,S) := S,
 i.e. m ρ = (V.weight (closedBall x ρ))⁻¹ • (V.measure.restrict (closedBall x ρ ×ˢ univ)).map Prod.snd.
(a) For every ρ and every f ∈ C(G,ℝ), ∫ f dm_ρ = avg_ρ^x(f). The ingredients are:
 - ∫ f d(t·ν) = t.toReal·∫ f dν for t ∈ [0,∞] (integral_smul_measure);
 - ∫ f d(σ_#ν') = ∫ f∘σ dν', since σ is measurable and f continuous (integral_map);
 - ∫ (f∘σ) d(V⌞(B × G)) = ∫_{B×G} f(z.2) dV;
 - (μ(B)⁻¹).toReal = (μ(B).toReal)⁻¹ (ENNReal.toReal_inv).
 Together they give ∫ f dm_ρ = (μ(B).toReal)⁻¹ ∫_{B×G} f(z.2) dV = avg_ρ^x(f). This holds for every ρ; no positivity is needed.
(b) For 0 < ρ < r, m_ρ is a probability measure: m_ρ(G) = μ(B_ρ(x))⁻¹·V(B_ρ(x) × G) = μ(B_ρ(x))⁻¹·μ(B_ρ(x)) = 1, since 0 < μ(B_ρ(x)) < ∞ by step 4 (Measure.map_apply, Measure.restrict_apply, Varifold.weight_apply, ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel).

6. Limits on the dense family (printed (4) for the β_j). Let j ∈ ℕ and 0 < ρ < r. By 5(b), every f ∈ C(G,ℝ) is m_ρ-integrable and ∫ c_j dm_ρ = c_j·m_ρ(G) = c_j. Hence ∫ f_j dm_ρ = ∫ β_j dm_ρ − c_j = avg_ρ^x(β_j) − c_j (integral_add, integral_const, and 5(a) for β_j).
 Since (0, r) ∈ 𝓝[>]0 and avg_ρ^x(β_j) → e_j(x) by (c), we get ∫ f_j dm_ρ → e_j(x) − c_j as ρ ↓ 0 (Tendsto.sub_const, Tendsto.congr'). So lim_{ρ↓0} ∫ f dm_ρ exists for every f in D := {f_1, f_2, …}, which is dense in C(G,ℝ).

7. Riesz limit (printed (3), (4) and the Riesz representation). Apply the sibling lemma riesz_limit with the nontrivial filter l := 𝓝[>]0 on ℝ, the family (m_ρ), and D. Its hypotheses hold: m_ρ is a probability measure for all ρ ∈ (0, r), hence l-eventually (step 5(b)); D is dense (step 1); and limits exist on D (step 6).
 It yields a probability measure η on G with ∫ f dm_ρ → ∫ f dη as ρ ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C(G,ℝ). By 5(a), avg_ρ^x(β) = ∫ β dm_ρ for all ρ, so avg_ρ^x(β) → ∫ β dη for every continuous β : G → ℝ. Since x was an arbitrary point of the μ-conull set of step 3, the statement holds for μ-a.e. x. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take a dense sequence f_j in the separable space C(G,ℝ) and set β_j := f_j + ‖f_j‖ ≥ 0.
slice_density for each β_j gives avg_ρ^x(β_j) → e_j(x) μ_V-a.e.; intersect with x ∈ U and x ∈ spt μ_V (countably many conull sets).
For such x, 0 < μ_V(B_ρ(x)) < ∞ for small ρ. The slice measures m_ρ = μ_V(B_ρ(x))⁻¹ σ_#(V⌞(B_ρ(x)×G)) satisfy ∫ f dm_ρ = avg_ρ^x(f) for every ρ and are eventually probability measures.
∫ f_j dm_ρ = avg_ρ^x(β_j) − ‖f_j‖ converges for every j.
riesz_limit gives a probability measure η with ∫ f dm_ρ → ∫ f dη for all f, i.e. avg_ρ^x(β) → ∫ β dη.

subproblems.title: Lemma 8.1.3, second part: ∫_{Gₙ(A)} β dV = ∫_A ∫ β dη^(x) dμ_V(x)
subproblems.statement: Let V be an n-varifold on an open set U ⊆ ℝ^N with weight μ_V. Let η : ℝ^N → Measure(G(N,n)) be such that, for μ_V-a.e. x, η(x) is a probability measure and (∫_{B_ρ(x)×G} β(S) dV(y,S)) / μ_V(B_ρ(x)) → ∫ β dη(x) as ρ ↓ 0 for every continuous β : G(N,n) → ℝ (closed balls; Bochner integral divided by μ_V(B_ρ(x)).toReal). Then for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^N and every continuous β ≥ 0 on G(N,n): ∫⁻_{A×G} ofReal(β(S)) dV(x,S) = ∫⁻_A (∫⁻ ofReal(β(S)) dη(x)(S)) dμ_V(x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (η : Euclidean N → Measure (Grassmannian N n)), (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, IsProbabilityMeasure (η x) ∧ ∀ β : C(Grassmannian N n, ℝ), Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ ↦ (∫ z in closedBall x ρ ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)), β z.2 ∂V.measure) / (V.weight (closedBall x ρ)).toReal) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (∫ S, β S ∂(η x)))) → ∀ (A : Set (Euclidean N)) (β : C(Grassmannian N n, ℝ)), MeasurableSet A → (∀ S, 0 ≤ β S) → ∫⁻ z in A ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)), ENNReal.ofReal (β z.2) ∂V.measure = ∫⁻ x in A, (∫⁻ S, ENNReal.ofReal (β S) ∂(η x)) ∂V.weight
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 8, end of the proof of Lemma 1.3 (p. 208): "Finally the last part of the lemma follows directly from (2) … if we keep in mind that e(x,j) in (1) is exactly η̃_V^(x)(β_j) ≡ ∫ β_j dη_V^(x)." This is step 5 of the parent proof, with one simplification: (2) is applied to the given β itself. Any fixed β ∈ 𝒦⁺ can be adjoined to the countable family β_1, β_2, …, so it plays the role of β_j. The uniform approximation by the β_{j_k} and the summation over compact pieces of U in the parent's step 5 are then unnecessary. The identity is stated with lintegrals for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^N (correction (c) of the parent proof).

Notation. G := G(N,n), μ := μ_V = V.weight, and avg_ρ^x(β) := (∫_{B_ρ(x)×G} β(z.2) dV)/μ(B_ρ(x)).toReal.

1. The printed (1)–(2) for β. Fix a Borel set A ⊆ ℝ^N and β ∈ C(G,ℝ) with β ≥ 0. The sibling lemma slice_density gives e : ℝ^N → ℝ with:
 (1) for μ-a.e. x, avg_ρ^x(β) → e(x) as ρ ↓ 0;
 (2) ∫⁻_{A×G} ofReal(β(S)) dV(y,S) = ∫⁻_A ofReal(e(x)) dμ(x).

2. "e(x,·) is exactly η̃^(x)(·)". By hypothesis, for μ-a.e. x, η(x) is a probability measure and avg_ρ^x(β) → ∫ β dη(x) as ρ ↓ 0. For μ-a.e. x this and (1) hold together. Since 𝓝[>]0 is a nontrivial filter on ℝ and ℝ is Hausdorff, limits are unique (tendsto_nhds_unique), so e(x) = ∫ β dη(x).

3. From Bochner integral to lintegral. For such x, β is continuous on the compact space G, hence bounded and Borel, hence integrable for the finite measure η(x) (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport, HasCompactSupport.of_compactSpace). As β ≥ 0, ofReal(∫ β dη(x)) = ∫⁻ ofReal(β(S)) dη(x)(S) (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal). Hence ofReal(e(x)) = ∫⁻ ofReal(β(S)) dη(x)(S) for μ-a.e. x.

4. Conclusion. Integrands that agree μ-a.e. have the same lintegral over the Borel set A (setLIntegral_congr_fun_ae; measurability of x ↦ ∫⁻ ofReal β dη(x) is not needed). So ∫⁻_A ofReal(e(x)) dμ(x) = ∫⁻_A (∫⁻ ofReal(β(S)) dη(x)(S)) dμ(x). Combined with (2): ∫⁻_{A×G} ofReal(β(S)) dV = ∫⁻_A (∫⁻ ofReal(β) dη(x)) dμ(x). ∎
proof_key_steps: slice_density for the given β ≥ 0: avg_ρ^x(β) → e(x) μ_V-a.e., and ∫⁻_{A×G} ofReal β dV = ∫⁻_A ofReal e dμ_V (printed (1)–(2)).
Uniqueness of limits along 𝓝[>]0 gives e(x) = ∫ β dη(x) μ_V-a.e. (printed "e(x,j) is exactly η̃^(x)(β_j)").
ofReal(∫ β dη(x)) = ∫⁻ ofReal β dη(x) for the probability measure η(x) and bounded β ≥ 0.
Replace the integrand μ_V-a.e. on A and combine with (2).
